In [[geometry]], the '''elongated pentagonal gyrobicupola''' is one of the [[Johnson solid]]s ({{math|''J''{{sub|39}}}}). As the name suggests, it can be constructed by elongating a [[pentagonal gyrobicupola]] ({{math|''J''{{sub|31}}}}) by inserting a [[decagonal prism]] between its congruent halves. Rotating one of the [[pentagonal cupola]]e ({{math|''J''{{sub|5}}}}) through 36&nbsp;degrees before inserting the prism yields an [[elongated pentagonal orthobicupola]]  ({{math|''J''{{sub|38}}}}).

{{Johnson solid}}

==Formulae==
The following [[formula]]e for [[volume]] and [[surface area]] can be used if all [[faces (geometry)|faces]] are [[regular polygon|regular]], with edge length ''a'':<ref>[[Stephen Wolfram]], "[http://www.wolframalpha.com/input/?i=Elongated+pentagonal+gyrobicupola Elongated pentagonal gyrobicupola]" from [[Wolfram Alpha]]. Retrieved July 25, 2010.</ref>

:<math>V=\frac{1}{6}\left(10+8\sqrt{5}+15\sqrt{5+2\sqrt{5}}\right)a^3\approx12.3423...a^3</math>

:<math>A=\left(20+\sqrt{\frac{5}{2}\left(10+\sqrt{5}+\sqrt{75+30\sqrt{5}}\right)}\right)a^2\approx27.7711...a^2</math>
